note: phase A — T[N] declaration with a full array literal; element type/length come from the annotation
phase A — no annotation; T[N] is inferred from the literal (element type from first element, N from element count)
phase A — empty array literal `[]` is rejected: neither element type nor length is inferable
phase A — literal has 3 elements but the T[4] context requires exactly 4
phase A — element types disagree (int32 then bool); remaining elements must match the first
phase A — element type disagrees with the int32[N] annotation

phase A — array length must be a compile-time integer literal, not a variable
phase A — T[0] is rejected; zero-length arrays are out of scope (decision 12)
phase A — negative length is rejected; only positive literal lengths are accepted
phase A — void is not a storable element type (§6.8)
phase A — compile-time literal index inside [0, N) is accepted (and the bounds check may be elided)
phase A — a[i] read yields T; literal index in range is fine
phase A — array elements participate in ordinary arithmetic once indexed
phase A — a compile-time literal index outside [0, N) is an analyzer error, NOT a runtime trap (decision 44)
phase A — index must be uintsize; a bool index is rejected
phase A — uint8 element type; integer literals in the array literal adopt the element type
phase A — bool[N] is byte-per-element per §6.6; element usable directly as a condition
phase A — char[N] with char-literal elements; char == comparison per §6.4
phase A — float64[N] with decimal-literal elements; float ordering per §5
phase A — a[i] = v write is permitted through a `let` array
phase A — element write through a `const` array is rejected
phase A — .length is a compile-time-known uintsize property

phase A — index `i` is a let bound to a constant literal (10); analyzeIndexExpression constant-folds the identifier and reports out-of-bounds at COMPILE time. Genuine runtime-trap coverage needs an index the analyzer cannot fold (a loop counter, or a value read at runtime)

phase A — write-path index `i` is a let bound to a constant literal (7); once the assignment path runs analyzeIndexExpression the identifier constant-folds and out-of-bounds is reported at COMPILE time
phase A — whole-array assignment between same-type arrays; value (copy) semantics
phase A — int32[3] and int32[4] are distinct types; whole-array assignment between them is rejected

phase A — element write to an array field through a `let` struct value
phase A — element write through a `const` struct is rejected, same as a direct const array
phase A — .length works on an array field (s.field.length)
phase A — an array field coexisting with scalar fields; inline storage, no indirection
phase A — bool[N] as a struct field (byte-per-element per §6.6)

phase A — array field on an inner struct, reached through a nested struct field (o.inner.data[i])

phase A — array-literal element type disagrees with the field's element type

phase A — a zero-length array field is rejected (decision 12)
